gloss: the following year; the next year

definitions.gloss: the following year; the year after a particular reference year
definitions.explanation: A written, somewhat formal way of saying "the year after" a previously mentioned year or event. Commonly appears in news articles, biographies, timelines, and historical or academic writing. Unlike {来年|らいねん} (next year from now), {翌年|よくねん} is relative to a reference point established in context — usually the year just mentioned.

examples.japanese: {翌年|よくねん}{結婚|けっこん}した。
examples.english: They got married the following year.

examples.japanese: {翌年|よくねん}の{春|はる}に{東京|とうきょう}へ{引|ひ}っ{越|こ}した。
examples.english: I moved to Tokyo in the spring of the following year.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{大学|だいがく}を{卒業|そつぎょう}し、{翌年|よくねん}には{大|おお}きな{会社|かいしゃ}に{就職|しゅうしょく}した。
examples.english: He graduated from university and, the following year, took a job at a large company.

examples.japanese: {地震|じしん}が{起|お}きたのは{1995年|せんきゅうひゃくきゅうじゅうごねん}で、{翌年|よくねん}から{本格的|ほんかくてき}な{復興|ふっこう}{作業|さぎょう}が{始|はじ}まった。
examples.english: The earthquake occurred in 1995, and full-scale reconstruction work began the following year.

notes:
A relative time noun meaning "the year after (a previously mentioned year)." The reference year must be established in context — {翌年|よくねん} does not mean "next year from now."

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {翌年|よくねん}の{春|はる}: the spring of the following year
- {翌年|よくねん}{3月|さんがつ}: March of the following year
- {翌年|よくねん}に{入|はい}る: to enter the following year
- {翌年|よくねん}から: starting the following year
- {翌年|よくねん}までに: by the following year

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {来年|らいねん}: next year — relative to the current year from the speaker's standpoint.
- {翌年|よくねん}: the following year — relative to a year previously mentioned in context.
- {明年|みょうねん}: next year — a more formal, written equivalent of {来年|らいねん}, used in letters and announcements.
- {翌|よく}{年度|ねんど}: the following fiscal year — used when talking about fiscal or academic years rather than calendar years.

REGISTER:
Written or semi-formal. Common in news, biographies, historical writing, official reports, and narrative descriptions of sequences of events. In casual conversation, Japanese speakers often use {次|つぎ}の{年|とし} (the next year) instead.

RELATED TIME NOUNS:
- {翌日|よくじつ}: the following day
- {翌週|よくしゅう}: the following week
- {翌月|よくげつ}: the following month
- {翌朝|よくあさ}: the following morning

These all follow the same pattern: {翌|よく} + time unit = "the following X." They all require a reference point from context.
